title: Cover Picture and Issue Information
content:
Cover image: The southern mallee Ctenotus (Ctenotus atlas), in front of the spinifex tussocks (Triodia scariosa) upon which it is entirely reliant. Spinifex tussocks in the South Australian Murray Mallee can provide shaded thermal refuges for reptiles, but their structure and cooling capacity are reduced after fire (Credit: Max Tibby)

This cover is provided by the authors of the article “Out of the fire and into the frying pan: Hostile post-fire thermal conditions reduce activity windows for reptiles” (https://doi.org/10.1111/1365-2435.70463), which features in this issue. They demonstrated that fire-driven structural simplification translates to weakened thermal refugia, with implications for species persistence under increasing heat extremes.
